# Maximum Units on a Truck.

@example Load the 3 boxes of 6 units and the 2 boxes of 4 units: 18 + 8 = 26. Nothing else fits.
[[2,4],[6,1],[3,6]]
5
=> 26

@example The 4 boxes of 5 units go first, then 3 of the 10 boxes of 3 units: 20 + 9 = 29.
[[10,3],[4,5]]
7
=> 29

@example All 3 boxes fit, so the truck takes them all: 9 + 2 + 2 = 13.
[[1,9],[2,2]]
50
=> 13

# The smallest input.
[[1,1]]
1
=> 1

# A single kind, with more boxes than fit, or fewer.
[[5,7]]
3
=> 21

[[5,7]]
9
=> 35

# A truck for one box takes the best box.
[[3,2],[1,8],[4,5]]
1
=> 8

# The kind with the most boxes, and the most units in all, is the worst
# choice: 2 boxes of 50 and 8 of 1 make 108.
[[200,1],[2,50]]
10
=> 108

# Kinds listed from the fewest units to the most.
[[4,1],[3,2],[2,3],[1,4]]
6
=> 16

# The truck is full exactly when the second best kind is used up.
[[3,9],[5,2],[4,6]]
7
=> 51

# The truck holds exactly the whole stock.
[[3,9],[5,2],[4,6]]
12
=> 61

# Equal units, and identical entries.
[[2,5],[3,5],[2,5],[1,9]]
6
=> 34

# The largest truck, with only 2000 boxes in stock.
[[1000,1000],[1000,999]]
1000000
=> 1999000

# A box of the second kind costs as much room as one of the first.
[[1000,1000],[1000,999]]
1500
=> 1499500

# Every value at its limit: 10^6 boxes of 1000 units, all of which fit.
# The answer, 10^9, still fits in an int; loading one box at a time and
# searching all 1000 kinds for each would take 10^9 steps.

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[[3,6],[3,3],[5,2]]
10
=> 35

@gen 2 small
[[3,3],[2,1],[2,1],[1,6],[3,4]]
10
=> 30

[[1,3],[3,2],[5,4],[1,1],[2,5],[3,2]]
4
=> 18

=> 41

2
